To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we determined the structure and biochemical properties of the Vibrio vulnifcus toxin effector domain RRSP, which is a bacterial protease that cleaves Ras, and we determined that the cleavage of Ras by RRSP does not release any fragments and does not dissociate Ras from its bound nucleotides but only locally affects its structure.
RRSP is an atypical protease that cleaves KRAS through an atypical, nucleotide-independent mechanism to disrupt KRAS–RAF signaling.

we solved the crystal structure and determined the catalytic residues of a bacterial Ras/Rap effector domain, that we determined the mechanism of action for the cleavage of KRAS by this effector domain, and that we showed that the cleavage of Ras by RRSP inhibits Ras signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the bacterial effector domain RRSP.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the virulence of pathogenic bacteria and their toxins.
the molecular mechanisms of Ras signaling and the regulation of this pathway by pathogenic bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bacterial toxin RRSP cleaves RAS through an atypical, metalloproteolytically inactive mechanism that results in structural changes in the RAS G domain that disrupts its interaction with its downstream effector, RAF.

RRSP is an atypical protease that cleaves Ras and disrupts Ras–extracellular-signal–regulated kinase signaling by inducing a structural change in Ras, rather than by releasing fragments or bound nucleotide.

RRSP is a novel protease that represents a previously unidentified class of proteases that disrupts Ras signaling by inducing minimal structural disturbance in its targets, which in turn prevents Ras from binding to its downstream effactors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we solved the structure and mechanism of a bacterial toxin effector, the Ras/Rap-specific protease (RRSP).
we identified a novel class of proteases and determined the mechanism by which they disrupt Ras signaling.
the bacterial effector RRSP cleaves RAS through an atypical proteolytic mechanism that disrupts its interaction with RAF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of Ras by RRSP does not release fragments or nucleotides but instead induces a local conformational change.
we identified the mechanism by which the bacterial toxin effector RRSP cleaves KRAS and inhibits Ras signaling.
RRSP is an unusual protease that cleaves KRAS at an atypical site and that the cleavage event does not release any fragments from KRAS but instead alters the structure of the protein.
